reason: E4 and E5 show that refractory HEAs can retain strength above 1200°C and that solid solution strengthening contributes, but E2 and E3 directly show that refractory additions can cause softening via impurity-induced precipitation, contradicting the premise that they reliably improve properties. The cited evidence is mixed and partly misrepresented.
premises: Refractory elements (Mo, Nb, Ta) increase high-temperature strength via solid solution strengthening
Solid solution strengthening is the dominant mechanism at elevated temperatures
